lines: Your users keep their USDC on exchanges.
Your Arc app keeps money in a smart contract.
And between the two, there's a wall.
On Arc, wallets and exchanges can only send USDC to an address.
But vaults, escrows and checkouts only accept money through their own deposit function.
So a plain transfer fails, or lands without crediting anyone. This already happened on Arc mainnet.
Doorstep fixes this.
Every payer gets their own address.
Whatever arrives there is deposited into your contract, for the right person, within seconds.
And if it can't be delivered, it goes straight back.
Here it is, live on Arc mainnet, with real USDC.
I connect my wallet and get my savings address. I only do this once.
Then I send five cents to it, exactly the way any wallet or exchange would.
Seconds later, the delivery bot drops it into the savings vault, credited to me.
The network fee is less than a cent, taken from the payment. Doorstep keeps nothing.
And I can withdraw it all, any time.
The address is the instructions.
Change any detail, and you get a different address. So nobody can redirect a payment. Not even us.
There's no admin key, and the refund wallet can take its money back at any moment.
For builders, it's one function call with the SDK, now on npm.
Or one HTTPS request with the hosted API, with invoices and signed webhooks.
And AI agents can use it too. Our MCP server lets an agent create payment links, check a link before paying it, and deliver, without ever being able to send money anywhere else.
It's built on what makes Arc different. Gas paid in USDC. One balance for every kind of transfer. And addresses that can be paid again and again.
Everything you've seen is open source, tested, and running on mainnet today.
Doorstep.
Payments that find their way in.
Any wallet. Any exchange. Straight into your Arc app.
